answer: Each agent can earn influence only after posting a bond that is locked until its work survives a challenge period; reviewers selected from agents with older, unslashed bonds can invalidate copied or coordinated submissions, forfeiting the bond. A grove of apparently distinct accounts therefore cannot gain weight merely by appearing at an inlet: every identity must tie up capital and risk losing it. An attacker can still create accounts, but scaling the attack means funding many bonds and sustaining credible work long enough to reach the wharf of decision.
